ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is dark brown to black with narrow, white, V-shaped crossbands and a distinct white collar. It features a flattened head and large, prominent eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lycodon gammiei* is best distinguished by its distinct, broad white nuchal collar and a series of white vertebral spots that fade into a reticulated pattern posteriorly.
ai.habitat: Lycodon gammiei inhabits the dense evergreen and broadleaf forests of the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Gammie's Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt small lizards and geckos among rocky crevices and forest leaf litter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon gammiei* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon gammiei* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim and West Bengal, typically inhabiting elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
